named_subject: a pig seen from the side, with a spiral snout, two pointed ears, a round body and short stick legs
action: The pig stands still in profile for six frames, then shrinks and slides right, then grows larger and tilts its body so the head drops lower and to the left while the legs spread.
identity_gap: The drawing keeps the doodle's spiral snout, zigzag ears, open body outline and split leg strokes, but in frames 11-16 the body is rotated and swollen so the outline proportions drift from the doodle.
notes: The film shows the pig standing, then turning its head toward the camera and walking forward so it grows larger in frame, but the animation first shrinks the pig in frames 8-9 and then rotates the whole flat side-view drawing instead of turning the head, and the size changes at frames 8, 9 and 11 read as pops. The one change that would help most is to remove the shrink in frames 7-9 and make the growth a steady increase across frames 7-16 so the pig scales up continuously as it approaches the camera.
